title: How much of a water-leak detector's score on the BattLeDIM benchmark beats random alarms?
lede: research programme: leak detection on the real BattLeDIM L-Town benchmark (2018 tunes, 2019 tests), scored against chance; step 1's data-driven residual CUSUM (no hydraulic model) finds 13 of the 19 leaks that start in 2019 with 2 false alarms, but the same number of random alarms finds a median 11 (P = 0.105), so a detection count alone barely says anything; the alarming pressure sensor is within 300 m of the leak for 5 of the 13, against a chance median of 0 (P < 0.001)
summary: An open research programme on leak detection and localisation in water distribution networks, run on the one public benchmark with a realistic network, two years of SCADA data and a published leak schedule: BattLeDIM's L-Town (Vrachimis et al. 2022; Zenodo 4017659, CC-BY-4.0), which infra-waterloss could not reach and replaced with Net3. It asks how much of a detector's reported skill is above what random alarms would score, and whether a data-driven detector can carry a false-alarm rate fixed before the year is seen. Step 1 (2026-11-12) builds the harness: SHA-256-checked loader, ground truth from the leak-flow files (onsets match Melnikov 2025's table), matching (an alarm counts for the running leak with the latest onset within 30 days) and distances along the pipe graph. Detector D1 fits each of the 33 pressure sensors on hour-of-week, tank level and the three inlet flows over a trailing two-week window ending a week back, runs a one-sided CUSUM on the standardised residuals, and re-anchors its window after each alarm (an earlier hold-off version re-alarmed on the same leak; a unit test caught it). Tuned on 2018 only (at most 2 false alarms), on 2019 it detects 13 of the 19 new leaks with 2 false alarms, a median delay of 104 h (11 to 341), and 16 of BattLeDIM's 23 counting the 3 of 4 carried-over leaks it found in 2018; without localisation, so not comparable with the published 15 to 17 of 23, which required a reported pipe within 300 m. Against the same 26 alarms placed at random (1,000 draws, 14 days apart, random sensors), the detection count is near chance (median 11, 95% range 8 to 13, P = 0.105), as is detection within 72 h (4 against 2, P = 0.145); but the alarming sensor is within 300 m along the pipes of 5 detected leaks against a chance median of 0 (P < 0.001). L-Town is a simulated network with simulated leaks; 2018 labels were used for tuning, which competitors did not have; nothing here is an operational recommendation.
